chunks: We then made the people who were weak (and oppressed) successors of the land to the East and the West which We had blessed. Thus the fair promise of your Lord to the children of Israel was fulfilled, for they were patient in adversity; and whatsoever the Pharaoh and his people had fashioned, and the structures they had raised, were destroyed.
ai.seo_question: What happened to the land and Pharaoh's structures according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the concept of 'warathah' (inheritance) not merely as physical possession but as the culmination of divine patience (sabr) against tyranny, foreshadowing the ultimate victory of the righteous. The destruction of Pharaoh's 'works' (ya'rishoon) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as the dismantling of the socio-political structures of oppression, establishing a precedent for the establishment of justice by the Ahl al-Bayt.
